newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela seeks to revive Russian oil swap-Arrieta.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela seeks to revive Russian oil swap-Arrieta.

text.p: Venezuela and Russia are working to revive an oil swap contract which operated until the collapse of the Soviet Union, Venezuela's Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Tuesday.
"It is part of the talks (between Venezuela and Russia)," Arrieta told reporters in Congress. "It would involve two producers and two consumers," he added.
Venezuela used to supply 20,000 barrels of crude per day to Cuba on behalf of the Soviet Union while Moscow supplied a similar quantity to Spain on behalf of Venezuela.
"These type of agreements have great advantages, such as the saving of transport costs," Arrieta said.
Arrieta has often cited the Venezuela-Russia oil swap deal to argue that the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries should reorganize itself along geographical lines.
Venezuela's Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Burelli Rivas is current on an official visit to Russia.
